# Shared-interface refinement (open; local work card)

Parent: `natural-hypercube-representation`. Proposed first transfer: the eight-state (3,8) chart, not all Ramsey systems. No change to the parent verdict.

**Conjecture.** A nonconstant natural coordinate on this chart can be generated by a source-defined two-reading interface: after suppressing one reading bit, a base address can admit reading 0, reading 1, or both. In each layer the address identifies the state uniquely. Exactly the doubly admissible addresses support bridges between equal addresses. On the overlap the induced moves in both layers agree. Splitting the shared addresses, restoring their two tags and bridges, and retaining within-layer moves reconstructs precisely the elementary transition graph. Both tagged halves are geodesically convex. Require relabeling covariance up to tag reversal and address renaming. For unweighted connected bipartite transitions test convexity by orienting each bridge 0 to 1: every target in layer 1 must get closer and every target in layer 0 farther. This is a one-axis conjecture; full cube metric requires a separating family of coordinates with all distances equal to Hamming distances.

**Known vs predicted.** In a full cube every address has both readings; in a partial cube the interface can be proper and need not be a connected plane. Retrospective replay on parent 3 minus sites 1,19 at (3,7) uses each of the two previously derived gate bits separately. Each has two 11-state layers on 18 base addresses; four addresses have both readings, with two disjoint shared edges, and all four bridges agree on target sides. See [checker](../chatgpt/ramsey/ramsey_interface_replay.py) and [counts](../chatgpt/ramsey/ramsey_interface_replay.json). Addresses here came from contracting the known bridges, not from a blind constructor. [Negative control](../chatgpt/ramsey/ramsey_target_gradient.json): four crossings of the failed bit in the 12-state boundary predict two different target partitions. Neither a legal four-group table nor a collection of commuting squares proves a convex cut.

**Next experiment, in order.** (1) On the (3,8) source, specify states, elementary move and any history needed for the readout. Freeze a source rule for the base address, both admissibility predicates and within-layer moves *before* inspecting target-distance partitions. Do not define the address by contracting the desired edges. (2) Generate predicted tagged states and transitions, compare bijectively to the chart, replay under relabelings, and report missing/spurious bridges or incompatible shared edges. (3) Test bridge-to-target distances; save the first contrary move and target. If that candidate fails, separately test intrinsic cuts to distinguish a wrong source rule from a noncubical graph. One failure rejects the rule, not all possible source constructions. Do not silently replace directed transitions by undirected ones.

**Assembly bridge, separate and open.** On a native particle-like assembly example, specify the permitted moves and continuation readout independently. Identifying two histories as one tagged state must preserve the readout after each admissible continuation. A common interface vocabulary alone establishes neither a Ramsey interpretation nor physical particle dynamics.
